author: Refract
description: Draft, approve and schedule social media posts from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other AI apps.
name: Refract

tools.name: list-workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: Lists the Refract workspaces this connection can use, with each one's time zone and permissions. Call it first: each workspace is a brand or client with its own accounts, its "workspace" value goes into the other tools, and "postsNeedApproval" says whether posts you send wait for a teammate.

tools.name: list-accounts
tools.title: List Accounts
tools.description: Lists the social accounts connected in a workspace. Use their "id" values to choose where a draft goes; "needsReconnect" marks accounts that can't post until someone reconnects them in Refract. A TikTok account also has "privacyLevelOptions": the choices TikTok gives it for who can view a post, for create-draft's privacy_level (null when TikTok can't be reached).

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

tools.name: list-posts
tools.title: List Posts
tools.description: Lists a workspace's posts, newest first, with their status and scheduled time. Filter by status or by a date range in the workspace's time zone. A post waiting for approval comes with its "approval": its id, who asked, when it would go out and whether a client decides it. Texts are cut at 280 characters (get-post has the whole post) and come inside <untrusted> tags.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

status.description: Only posts with this status, e.g. draft or scheduled.

from.description: Only posts scheduled on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: Only posts scheduled on or before this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

limit.description: How many posts to return, from 1 to 50; 20 by default.

tools.name: get-post
tools.title: Get Post
tools.description: Gets one post with its text, accounts and their status, media, scheduled time and history. Per-platform texts and the media ids each platform leaves off are included where they differ. An account that failed comes with its "failure": what went wrong, in plain words, and the "fix" it offers (retry, shrink_and_retry, crop_and_retry, reconnect, edit_post or none). A post waiting for approval comes with its "approval": its id, who asked, when it would go out and whether a client decides it. Text people or networks wrote comes inside <untrusted> tags.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The post's id (a UUID), from list-posts or create-draft.

tools.name: check-post
tools.title: Check Post
tools.description: Runs the composer's checks on a saved post and lists its issues per platform, each with a sentence. Severity "block" stops the post from being scheduled; "warn" and "info" are worth a look. Use it before scheduling a long post, a post with media, or one for several networks.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The post's id (a UUID), from create-draft or list-posts.

tools.name: read-analytics
tools.title: Read Analytics
tools.description: Reads a workspace's analytics for a period: totals against the period before, each network's numbers, the best posts and gaps. The best posts are the top 5 by views and by engagement rate; gaps are plain sentences about missing data. Use range 7d, 30d or 90d (30d by default), or from and to for exact days within the plan's history. A number a network doesn't report is null, not zero: say it isn't reported, never that it is 0. Engagement rate is engagements divided by views (0.042 is 4.2%). Post texts are cut at 200 characters and come inside <untrusted> tags. link opens the analytics page for the same period.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

range.description: The last 7, 30 or 90 days up to today; 30d by default. Leave out when you give from and to.

from.description: The first day of an exact period (YYYY-MM-DD), in the workspace's time zone. Give to as well. Days before the plan's analytics history are refused with the earliest day allowed.

to.description: The last day of an exact period (YYYY-MM-DD), today or earlier. Give from as well.

platforms.description: Only these networks, e.g. ["instagram", "linkedin"]. Leave out for every network.

accounts.description: Only these accounts: ids from list-accounts. Leave out for every account.

tools.name: find-slots
tools.title: Find Slots
tools.description: Finds the next free posting times for some accounts: the workspace's posting times (its queue) that none of them uses yet, in the workspace's time zone. schedule-post without "at" takes the first one.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

accounts.description: Ids of the accounts the post would go to, from list-accounts; a time is free when none of them has a post then.

count.description: How many free times to return, from 1 to 10; 3 by default.

after.description: Only times after this, in the workspace's time zone (e.g. "2026-10-19 00:00" for next Monday on). Leave out to start from now.

tools.name: create-draft
tools.title: Create Draft
tools.description: Creates a draft post in a workspace with its text, accounts and optional media. Per platform it can take a different text and the network's post fields (a title, tags, a community); nothing goes out until the draft is scheduled or approved.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

text.description: The post's text, shared by every platform unless "variants" says otherwise.

accounts.description: Ids of the accounts the post goes to, from list-accounts; at least one.

media.description: Ids of images or videos from upload-media or request-media-upload, in the order they appear in the post.

variants.description: Per platform where it differs from the main post: its text, or {"text", "settings", "skipped_media"} to set the network's post fields too (leave out "text" to keep the main text), e.g. {"x": "Shorter text for X", "youtube": {"settings": {"title": "Cupping at Kolo", "tags": ["coffee", "guji"]}}}. "skipped_media" lists ids from "media" that this platform leaves off, e.g. {"x": {"skipped_media": ["<id of the fifth file>"]}} when the network takes fewer files. Keys: instagram, facebook, threads, tiktok, youtube, linkedin, x, pinterest, bluesky, mastodon, telegram, google_business, wordpress. Post fields each platform takes: youtube: title, tags; pinterest: title; wordpress: title, tags. tags is a list, as_draft is true or false, post_as is {"name", "avatar_media_id"} with a picture from upload-media or request-media-upload. Some networks need a field, such as a title, before the post can be scheduled; a field a network doesn't take is refused. TikTok needs "privacy_level" in its settings before it can be scheduled: who can view the post, one of its account's privacyLevelOptions from list-accounts (PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE is Everyone, MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS is Friends, FOLLOWER_OF_CREATOR is Followers, SELF_ONLY is Only me). TikTok requires the person to pick it: ask them who can view the post and pass their answer, e.g. {"tiktok": {"settings": {"privacy_level": "PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE"}}}. Never choose it for them.

tools.name: update-draft
tools.title: Update Draft
tools.description: Changes a post that hasn't gone out yet: its text, its text and post fields per platform, its accounts or its media. Works on drafts, scheduled posts and posts waiting for approval; only what you pass changes, and a scheduled post keeps its time. Use it to edit a post instead of creating a new draft.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The post's id (a UUID), from create-draft or list-posts.

text.description: The whole new main text, shared by every platform without its own. Leave out to keep it.

accounts.description: Ids of all the accounts the post goes to from now on, from list-accounts; at least one. Leave out to keep them.

media.description: Ids of all the images or videos in the post from now on, in order (from get-post, upload-media or request-media-upload); [] removes them all. Leave out to keep them.

variants.description: Only the platforms whose own version changes: a text replaces that platform's text; {"text", "settings", "skipped_media"} replaces only the keys you pass ("text": null uses the main text again, "settings" changes only the fields you name); null drops the platform's own text and post fields. E.g. {"x": "Shorter text for X", "youtube": {"settings": {"title": "Cupping at Kolo"}}, "linkedin": null}. Keys: instagram, facebook, threads, tiktok, youtube, linkedin, x, pinterest, bluesky, mastodon, telegram, google_business, wordpress. Post fields each platform takes: youtube: title, tags; pinterest: title; wordpress: title, tags. tags is a list, as_draft is true or false, post_as is {"name", "avatar_media_id"} with a picture from upload-media or request-media-upload. Some networks need a field, such as a title, before the post can be scheduled; a field a network doesn't take is refused. TikTok needs "privacy_level" in its settings before it can be scheduled: who can view the post, one of its account's privacyLevelOptions from list-accounts (PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE is Everyone, MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS is Friends, FOLLOWER_OF_CREATOR is Followers, SELF_ONLY is Only me). TikTok requires the person to pick it: ask them who can view the post and pass their answer, e.g. {"tiktok": {"settings": {"privacy_level": "PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE"}}}. Never choose it for them.

tools.name: upload-media
tools.title: Upload Media
tools.description: Adds an image or video to a workspace's media library from a public link, or from a file the person attached in ChatGPT. Returns the media id to pass to create-draft or update-draft. For a file on disk or in your code sandbox, use request-media-upload instead.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

url.description: A public http or https link straight to the image or video file, e.g. https://example.com/photo.jpg. Leave out when you pass "file".

file.description: A file the person attached in the chat, in apps that pass attached files to tools (ChatGPT). Leave out when you pass "url".

download_url.description: Where Refract downloads the file from.

file_id.description: The file's id in the app it was attached in.

tools.name: request-media-upload
tools.title: Request Media Upload
tools.description: Gives a one-time link for uploading an image or video from your disk or code sandbox, such as a file the person attached in the chat. Run the returned curl command with the file's real path; its JSON answer has the media id to pass to create-draft or update-draft. The link stores one file and works for 15 minutes; a file Refract refuses doesn't use it up. For a file at a public link, use upload-media instead.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

tools.name: send-for-approval
tools.title: Send For Approval
tools.description: Sends a draft to the team for approval, to go out at a time you pick or at the workspace's next free posting time. Someone on the team approves it before it is published.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The draft's id (a UUID), from create-draft or list-posts.

at.description: When it should go out once approved, in the workspace's time zone (e.g. "2026-10-15 09:00"). Leave out for the next free posting time.

tools.name: schedule-post
tools.title: Schedule Post
tools.description: Schedules a draft to go out at a time you pick or at the workspace's next free posting time. When the workspace requires approval for AI tools, the draft is sent for approval instead; the answer's "status" says which.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The draft's id (a UUID), from create-draft or list-posts.

at.description: When it goes out, in the workspace's time zone (e.g. "2026-10-15 09:00"). Leave out for the next free posting time.

tools.name: publish-now
tools.title: Publish Now
tools.description: Publishes a draft or a scheduled post now, on every account it goes to. It can't be undone: ask the person first. When the workspace requires approval for AI tools, the post is sent for approval instead; the answer's "status" says which.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The post's id (a UUID), from create-draft or list-posts.

tools.name: reschedule-post
tools.title: Reschedule Post
tools.description: Moves a scheduled post, or one waiting for approval, to a new time in the workspace's time zone. A post waiting for approval keeps waiting, for the new time; for a draft, use schedule-post.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The scheduled post's id (a UUID), from list-posts.

at.description: The new time, in the workspace's time zone (e.g. "2026-10-15 09:00"); it must be in the future.

tools.name: unschedule-post
tools.title: Unschedule Post
tools.description: Takes a scheduled post, or one waiting for approval, off the schedule and back to the drafts. It keeps its text, accounts and media; a waiting approval request is withdrawn.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The scheduled post's id (a UUID), from list-posts.

tools.name: delete-draft
tools.title: Delete Draft
tools.description: Deletes a draft, or a post waiting for approval (its approval request goes too). A scheduled post must be taken off the schedule first with unschedule-post; posts that went out can't be deleted here.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The draft's id (a UUID), from create-draft or list-posts.

tools.name: edit-published-post
tools.title: Edit Published Post
tools.description: Changes the text and settings of a published post on one of its accounts. Works only where the network allows edits and within its time limit; when the workspace requires approval for AI tools, the edit waits for a teammate, and the answer's "state" says which ("applying" or "approving").

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The published post's id (a UUID), from list-posts.

account.description: The id (a UUID) of the account to edit it on, from the post's "accounts" in get-post.

text.description: The whole new text for that account; null for none, where the network takes a post without text (a title or media carry it).

settings.description: Settings for networks that take them, as the API names them: title, tags (list), community_id, canonical_url, as_draft, post_as ({name, avatar_media_id}). Leave out to keep the current settings.

tools.name: remove-published-post
tools.title: Remove Published Post
tools.description: Removes a published post from the network of one of its accounts. Ask the person before you call this: it only works where the network lets apps remove posts, the post stays in Refract marked removed, and its other accounts keep it.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The published post's id (a UUID), from list-posts.

account.description: The id (a UUID) of the account to remove it from, from the post's "accounts" in get-post.

tools.name: retry-post
tools.title: Retry Post
tools.description: Sends a post again to one account where it failed, and only that account. get-post shows each failed account's "failure": when its fix is shrink_and_retry or crop_and_retry, the files are fixed first; otherwise it's sent as it is, so change the text or settings with update-draft first when the failure is about them. It publishes at once and can't be undone: ask the person first. A signed-out account must be reconnected in Refract first.

workspace.description: The workspace's "workspace" value (its slug) from list-workspaces; its id works too.

post.description: The post's id (a UUID), from list-posts or get-post.

account.description: The id of the account where it failed, from get-post.
